Welcome to BURN Recon — here to reconcile the NAV-ERP BoM against what production actually does on the floor.
Take a quick tour?
Twelve short steps through the system, about two minutes. You can stop at any point and replay it later from the Guide tab.

Home

Where things stand, and the way into whatever needs attention. Every figure is live — a tile showing nothing to do is as useful as one showing a number.

Products being checked

Add a pair of BoMs per product — they are all verified together and reported as one.

Load the two records

The NAV BoM is the baseline; the floor record is what is actually consumed.

People & invitations

Who uses the system, and their work email.
NameWork email RoleFunctionInvitedCredential
Email invite opens your own mail client with the message written for you — the system cannot send mail itself. The invitation carries the file location, their role, how to get started and the rights they hold, but deliberately not the password. Send that separately; passwords in email outlive the person who needed them.

Access rights

Visible to admins only. Grant a user any of these when they need it, and withdraw it afterwards. 0 currently granted.

Share with the team

Hand the whole audit to a colleague, or pick up theirs.
The session file carries every product, floor record, drawing capture, scrap rate and decision. Send it with this HTML file and a colleague sees exactly what you see. For read-only sharing use the Excel or PDF report on All products instead. Everything stays on your machines — there is no server, so two people cannot edit the same audit at once; hand the file back and forth, or keep it on a shared drive.

Floor BoM —

Drawings —

The item number is the part number, and the part number is the drawing number — a trailing letter on it is the revision (11090D = drawing 11090 rev D). Type the number the line is actually building to; the revision is read off it. Same family with a different letter is a wrong revision; a different family is a different part. Every drawing is presumed correct until you amend it here.
ItemMaterial / description Approved part / drawingApproved rev Part / drawing in useRev in use StatusWhat is not okayDo what?
Load the NAV BoM and the floor record.

Scrap factors —

NAV carries no scrap allowance. The audit measures what the line really consumes; the difference is the scrap, which is then proposed back to NAV. Varies by item.
Any scrap the audit finds is reported, because NAV allows none. The standard above is only used to judge whether the observed rate is in line with expectation. Above the plausible ceiling it is treated as a utilization error rather than scrap.

Raw material master

Two ways to fill this. Upload the material list from NAV takes a file exported straight from NAV — use this to replace the master with the items currently in use, and to drop the obsolete ones. Pick them out of the loaded BoMs builds a master only from the products loaded here, matching your chosen terms; useful for a quick start, but it can never contain a material no loaded BoM mentions. Weights and scrap factors are held once here and every product cross-references them.
These terms apply only to picking materials out of the loaded BoMs. An uploaded NAV list is taken whole — every row with an item number is a material, whatever its description says.
ItemDescriptionUoM Unit weightSheet weight & rateUnit costScrap %Category Consumed byUtilization per product

Lines & work centres

Every line ranked by the audit work recorded against it. Audit coverage shows which lines have actually been walked — a line at 0% has findings that mean nothing yet.

Raised today

What this shift turned up, the products affected, and which products are running.

What the deviations cost

Each material deviation priced per product and per unit built, across every product it reaches — active and closed.

Work orders against the BoMs

The cost difference per product, and the whole variance summed across every BoM.

Sheet control

Sheet consumption against the scrap factor allowed for it, across the BoM, the floor, and every work order released and posted. Every material is covered; sheets are listed first because a sheet line going wrong costs more than anything else on the product.

Weekly, monthly and yearly position

What is still open, what it is worth in both currencies, which products carry it — archived ones included — and which work orders are affected.

Savings

What the system has caught — month by month at the top, then every finding priced line by line. A finding appears from the moment it is raised; only a closed one counts as recovered, and sheet is named separately throughout because that is where the money is.

Item quantities

How much of each item a product carries, compared across every product that uses it.

The group

Kenya, Nigeria, Tanzania, Ghana and Malawi — the same products, compared plant by plant.

BoM quality

How much of each BoM is in question, as a share of the lines it carries.

Value of the corrections

What each approved BoM correction is worth in cost, quality and risk averted.

Work order BoMs

Each production order checked against the NAV Product BoM it was raised from.

Pending issues

Every finding tracked from raised, through the teams and the approvals, to the NAV correction that closes it.

Document links

Point the system at where each Change Request Form and the material master live, instead of importing copies.

NAV scrap allowance to be added

Items whose scrap factor is held in the material master but not in the NAV BoM. NAV is understated on each — send this to the BoM team.

Material demand across products

Which materials the loaded products actually call for, ranked by how many need them. The ones on every BoM are the lines that stop production everywhere if they run out.

Cross-product coverage

Pick two to five products — any products, related or not — to see which items every one carries and which are missing from some. Costed where the material master holds a unit cost.

Family check

Products sharing a model code — KE_WB3.2 RW-AVSI and KE_WB3.2 LIKANO-RW are both WB3.2. Parts, drawings and their utilization must match; serialisation, leaflets and packaging may differ.
Everything uploaded from NAV is taken as correct. Run a comparison check to surface discrepancies, generate the report, and once an admin approves it the amendments appear on each product's BoM changes list.

Temporary process deviations

Temporary changes with an expiry. The stand-in material named here is the authorised reference, so while the TPD is open the difference is covered rather than reported. When it closes the SKU reverts to the BoM verified on NAV.
